title: 1993 AHSME Problem 20
statement: Consider the equation \(10z^2-3iz-k=0,\) where \(z\) is a complex variable and \(i^2=-1.\) Which of the following statements is true?

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text:
For all positive real numbers \(k,\) both roots are pure
imaginary.

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text:
For all negative real numbers \(k,\) both roots
are pure imaginary.

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text:
For all pure imaginary numbers \(k,\) both roots are real and
rational.

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text:
For all pure imaginary numbers \(k,\) both roots are real and
irrational.

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: For all complex numbers \(k,\) neither root is real.

solutions.text: The roots are \[ z=\frac{3i\pm\sqrt{-9+40k}}{20}. \] If \(k\) is negative and real, then \(-9+40k\) is negative real, so its square roots are pure imaginary. Both resulting values of \(z\) are therefore pure imaginary. The other universal claims fail, for example by taking \(k=1,\) \(i,\) or \(0\) as appropriate. Thus the correct answer is B.
hints: Apply the quadratic formula and simplify the discriminant
For negative real \(k,\) determine the type of \(\sqrt{-9+40k}\)
